 Telehealth Access to Mifepristone — Evaluating Reproductive-Coercion Arguments 
 E. Tobin-Tyler and G. Chalker
 Antiabortion advocates have asserted that mifepristone must be prescribed in person to prevent reproductive coercion, specifically forced abortions. But this argument targets the wrong culprit. Read the article.

 Maximizing Legal Care under Bans on Abortion Provision — A Framework for Reclaiming Agency 
 R. Jensen and Others
 In states with abortion bans, clinicians and hospitals should reduce harm by maximizing care to the extent legally possible, thereby recentering medical expertise and commitment to patient-centered care. Read the article.

 Human–Animal Bonds as Social Determinants of Health Care Access 
 R.M. Moore and R. Jagsi
 Clinicians who overlook patients’ relationships with their pets may both miss opportunities to improve health and misinterpret health care decisions that are constrained by competing obligations. Read the article. 
 PERSPECTIVE
 Safe Space 
 A.S. Pawar
 Physicians’ interactions with patients and their interactions with colleagues differ far more in the United States than they do in some other countries. Could more porous boundaries improve U.S. care? Read the article.
